# rest-design

Resource modelling, method semantics, status codes, idempotency and collection handling per HTTP semantics and common API style guides.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-REST-001` — Resources are plural nouns, not verbs (low)

`/orders` names the collection the method acts on; `/getOrders` encodes RPC in the URL and makes the uniform interface meaningless — caching, authorization-by-resource and client generation all degrade.

Remediation: Rename action-shaped paths to noun resources; move actions behind a dedicated sub-resource (`/orders/{id}/cancel`) or a custom method only when no CRUD verb fits.

Reference: https://restfulapi.net/resource-naming/

### `AF-REST-002` — HTTP methods carry their semantics (medium)

GET must be safe, PUT/DELETE idempotent, POST the non-idempotent create/process verb. Clients, caches, gateways and retry layers assume it; a GET that mutates can fire through prefetch alone.

Remediation: Move side effects off GET/HEAD; make repeated PUT/DELETE calls converge to one state; treat POST as the only non-idempotent verb.

Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-methods

### `AF-REST-003` — Status codes describe outcomes, not transport (medium)

200-everything forces clients to parse bodies to learn failure; 201 on create (with `Location`), 204 on bodyless success, 400 vs 422 vs 409 distinguish validation from conflict — middleware can then act on status alone.

Remediation: Return the most specific 2xx/4xx/5xx; never embed error codes inside a 200 payload; keep 5xx for faults the client cannot fix.

Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-status-codes

### `AF-REST-004` — Collections are paginated by contract (high)

An unbounded list endpoint is a memory/latency cliff decided by data growth, not by design. Pagination is breaking to add later — it must exist in the contract from the first version.

Remediation: Adopt cursor pagination (`cursor`, `limit`, `next`) for growing sets; offset only for bounded admin views; document the page contract.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-REST-005` — Unsafe operations accept idempotency keys (medium)

Clients retry POST on timeouts; without an `Idempotency-Key` the same logical request can create two orders. Stripe-style keys make retries safe by contract.

Remediation: Accept `Idempotency-Key` on POST; persist the key->response mapping with a TTL; replay the stored response on duplicate keys.

Reference: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header/

### `AF-REST-006` — Errors follow Problem Details (RFC 9457) (low)

Ad-hoc error shapes (`{"error": "x"}`) cannot be consumed generically; `application/problem+json` gives `type`/`title`/`status`/`detail`/ `instance` every client library already understands.

Remediation: Emit problem+json for 4xx/5xx; register `type` URIs for domain errors; keep `detail` free of secrets and stack traces.

Reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457

### `AF-REST-007` — Versioning is a declared strategy, not an accident (medium)

Mixing `/v1` prefixes, media-type versions and silent field changes in one API makes the compatibility contract unanswerable — consumers cannot tell what is stable.

Remediation: Pick one strategy (URI prefix recommended for HTTP APIs), apply it uniformly, and record the deprecation policy next to the contract.

Reference: docs/decisions/ADR-002-api-ir-provenance.md

### `AF-REST-008` — Trailing-slash semantics are significant and consistent (low)

`/orders` and `/orders/` are different resources to routers, caches and the API-IR; silently treating them as equal hides drift between contract and code (AF-CONTRACT/AF-CODE findings already treat them as distinct).

Remediation: Choose one canonical form per resource; redirect the other form rather than serving it; keep contract paths identical to served paths.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-design.md
